newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel up $1/bbl in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Diesel up $1/bbl in thin trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil chalked up an impressive near $1.00 per barrel gain on Thursday as the market rose for the fourth successive day, leaving many to ponder the unexpected strength, traders said.
Traders said the initial market hike was due to traders looking to cover physical short sales to Indonesia for August delivery cargoes.
The physical purchases were accompanied by a surge in swap prices as players covered short position and as others played the East-West spread, traders said.
Market strength was also put down to expectations of Chinese buying, following the crackdown on smuggling which has lead to increased domestic sales, resulting in lower stocks.
But even with these factors, many said market fundamentals did not justify such a hefty increase.
"People are puzzled with the strength," one trader said.
"China is still not buying and the (storage) tanks are still full in Singapore. I don't see any reason for prices to increase so much," another trader said.
Singapore middle distillate stocks for the week ending July 23 rose by 469,000 barrels to 11.084 million, the Trade Development Board said earlier.

In the physical market late Thursday a Dutch trader bought a 150,000-barrel cargo from a European major at $22.75 per barrel, up 85 cents from Wednesday's traded high of $21.90 and $1.45 more than the traded low of $21.30.
Traders said the Dutch trader might have bought his last cargo to cover earlier sales to Indonesia. The trader had bought four cargoes during the past week, they said.
The jump in physical prices was initiated by a similar large increase in the swaps market.
August swaps traded earlier in the day at $23.30, $23.35 and $23.40 before easing to last quote at $23.10/$23.20 per barrel, up from Wednesday $22.40/$22.50 per barrel, brokers said.
The sharp hike in August prices has narrowed the August/September spread to last trade at minus 44 cents and 48 cents from an early week trade of minus 70 cents, brokers said.
The jet fuel market also rose in tandem with firmer gas oil as several players came out to offer a total of five cargoes with the lowest at $24.50 per barrel for August 8-12 lifting.
The lowest offer was well above the $23.40 traded level on Tuesday.
But the firmer gas oil prices did lead to a narrowing of the swaps jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade with August last quoted at $1.40/$1.50 from Wednesday's $1.60/$1.80, brokers said.
August traded earlier in the day at $1.40, they said.
